missing_mechanism.requirement: An independently reviewed mechanism that (a) proves the exact OpenML datasets for the six OpenML nodes (breast_w, ionosphere, wdbc, credit_approval, sonar, climate) are available offline, bound to the exact task/data identity, and (b) enforces no network download in worker subprocesses while preserving the frozen worker's numerical semantics.
missing_mechanism.what_the_driver_checks: For a real run it refuses the whole case set when any case's node starts with 'openml_' (lines 578-579), before scheduling anything. Per case, execute_case independently refuses an OpenML case (lines 482-483); the only offline evidence it would accept is has_cache_files() (lines 434-436), i.e. the presence of any non-placeholder file under the node's data_cache, copied from the collector's PILOT_DATA_CACHE if absent (lines 495-501).
missing_mechanism.why_that_is_insufficient: M3 independent review of 4 November 2026 (Major 1) found that this presence-only test is not proof: a data_cache containing only an unrelated file returns has_cache_files() == True, the pinned harness 6adf385 node benchmark.py calls fetch_openml(..., data_home=...) without download_if_missing=False or another demonstrated network denial, so a partial or unrelated cache could pass preflight and start an attempted download in the worker. The same review's re-check states the hard STOP 'does not prove offline availability or implement the 16-case replay'; gate A1 is OPEN/partial and A4 (offline) is OPEN, and the offline mechanism and its independent review remain required. The 9 November review of the accepted M3 overnight unit states: 'Wiring into c3_env_replay.run is correctly left out; the production OpenML STOPs are unchanged.'
missing_mechanism.authorization_effect: The authorization retains this hard STOP and forbids bypass. Consequently no actual replay of the 16 fixed cases was possible, and the zero-tolerance PASS rule could not be evaluated.
